topic.title: Juniper ARP, IPv6 ND, and Layer 2 Resolution Troubleshooting
topic.scope: Covers Layer 2 next-hop MAC resolution across physical interfaces (ge-, xe-, ae), IRB/VLAN interfaces on Access/Aggregation nodes, and subscriber pseudowires (ps*) on L2 BNGs.

diagnosticChecklist.item: IP address and CIDR subnet mask configuration match on both ends of the segment.
Interface operational state is UP/UP (`show interfaces terse`).
ARP/ND entry status: Valid state vs. Incomplete/Hold state.
VLAN tagging, IRB binding, or Q-in-Q configuration on Access and Aggregation switches.
Duplicate IP address conflicts reported in syslog.
MAC address learning across intermediate L2 access switches (`show ethernet-switching table`).
Firewall filters (`family inet filter`) blocking ARP/ICMP traffic on the interface.

bngSubscriberResolution.description: On L2 BNGs, dynamic subscriber sessions terminate on logical units or pseudowires (ps*). If the subscriber route is active in the RIB but traffic fails:
bngSubscriberResolution.step: Verify subscriber access pseudowire state: `show interfaces ps<N>.<unit>`.

Verify ARP / subscriber binding entry, filtered to just this interface/unit: `show arp no-resolve interface ps<N>.<unit>` — no-resolve skips a reverse-DNS lookup per entry, which matters on a BNG with many subscribers. A broader `show arp | match ps` also works but returns every subscriber on the device, not just this one, and `show dhcp server binding` / `show pppoe subscriber` are the session-layer alternatives if the ARP entry itself is missing entirely.
Confirm the BNG has bound the subscriber IP to the correct underlying logical unit/MAC.
bngSubscriberResolution.psInterfaceLocation: A ps* interface lives on the PE/BNG layer, not the Metro access switch — `show arp no-resolve interface ps<N>.<unit>` must be run against whichever of these devices actually hosts the interface, not guessed: 197.155.94.100, 197.155.94.138, 41.175.38.42, 41.175.38.43. If the exact device isn't already known, try each candidate in turn until one reports the interface — the same candidate-device approach documented in show_interface_unit_syntax.xml for this same device set.
bngSubscriberResolution.psInterfaceNaming: A ps* interface's number and its logical unit number are always the same value — e.g. ps4411.4411, never ps4411.<a-different-number>. So given only a unit number (no interface name), the full interface reference can be constructed directly as ps<unit>.<unit> without a separate lookup step.

topic.ruleOfThumb: If the IP route exists in the routing table but neighbor resolution shows "Incomplete" or missing MAC entries, isolate Layer 2 VLAN tagging, physical link errors, subscriber session state, or firewall filtering rather than troubleshooting IS-IS/BGP routing protocols.
